title: Recurrent pressure rise — 90-second branching decision video
decisionPoint: Rising ventilator pressures and reduced right-sided air entry. Tracheostomy patent; ordinary suction retrieves little. End before clinical outcome.
requirements: camera at or below Rohan’s eye level when addressing him
no family member answers on his behalf

shotList.description: Wide orientation of the ICU room in daylight. Equipment present, not dominant.
Ventilator display showing a rising pressure trend — no flashing effects; steady readable numbers.
Clinician checks circuit and tracheostomy connection; suction yields little.
Camera at or below eye level. Rohan uses auditory scanning to report RIGHT MIDDLE.
Simplified animated overlay of possible distal plug (reuse Prompt 4 visual language: hatch + labels).
Clinician explains uncertainty to Rohan. Samira visible, not answering.
Three on-screen learner options: early bronchoscopy; targeted clearance and observation; aggressive pressure recruitment.

productionScript.speaker: AD
productionScript.text: Wide paediatric ICU bay. Daylight. Rohan in bed on controlled ventilation.

productionScript.speaker: AD
productionScript.text: Ventilator trend: pressures climbing steadily. No flashing.

productionScript.speaker: Clinician
productionScript.text: Circuit is connected. The tracheostomy tube is patent. Suction brings up very little.

productionScript.speaker: Clinician
productionScript.text: Rohan — auditory scan is on. Tell us the location when you hear it.

productionScript.speaker: AD
productionScript.text: Overlay: open central airway; possible distal plug with hatch pattern; reduced aeration beyond.

productionScript.speaker: Clinician
productionScript.text: We are uncertain. It may be a distal plug. It may be collapse or inflammation. We will not guess a pneumothorax without findings.

productionScript.speaker: AD
productionScript.text: Three learner options appear. Samira stays silent. Outcome not shown.

productionScript.speaker: ONSCREEN
productionScript.text: A Early bronchoscopy · B Targeted clearance and observation · C Aggressive pressure recruitment
